the marginal rate of preference of electric utility shareholders during the period 1958-66 averaged 5.4% per annum, and that the average risk aversion coefficient was 1.5.
the marginal rate of preference and risk aversions of investors in electric utilities are, respectively, 0.06 and 1.0.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an econometric model which is capable of explaining the valuation of electric utilities shares.
the development of an empirical model of the capital market for electric utility shares.

the development of a model of the valuation process which is consistent with the positive theory of the capital market, and which can yield estimates of the marginal cost of equity to the individual firm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides a more accurate measure of the marginal rate and risk aversion of electric utility share investors than has previously been available.
the marginal cost of equity for electric utilities ranges from 7.4 to 10.7 per cent.
the Sharpe-Linter model of the valuation and pricing of risk assets is a valuable tool in analyzing the capital markets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the empirical findings are in general consistent with the theoretical model and that the estimates of the marginal cost of equity for electric utilities are sensitive to changes in operating risk and to the level of risk aversion.

, within the framework of the Sharpe-Linter theory, investors in electric utility securities have been found to be risk-averse, to have a positive rate of time preference, and to be willing to pay for risk.
the empirical results are consistent with the theoretical predictions of the Sharpe-Linter capital market theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost of capital of the average utility is not a meaningful statistic.
there is a wide range of cost of equity estimates for the electric utility industry.
the cost of equity to electric utilities varies considerably, depending upon the firm's operating risk.
